findings.title: Failed work is marked complete and its offset can be committed
findings.body: When `result_processor` raises, this handler logs the exception but the `finally` block still calls `complete_offset`. The commit loop can therefore commit past a message whose processing failed, so Kafka will not redeliver it after a restart. Leave failed offsets outstanding or route them through the consumer's failure/DLQ handling before marking them complete.

findings.title: Offset gaps can prevent commits indefinitely
findings.body: This loop requires every integer offset between the lowest and highest observed offset to be present in `all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not guaranteed to be consecutive among delivered records: compacted records and broker/control records can leave gaps. If an offset is skipped, the tracker will refuse to commit any later completed records for that partition indefinitely, eventually causing reprocessing and stalled progress. Track delivery order/commit safety without requiring every numeric offset to have been delivered.

findings.title: Shutdown relies on Queue.shutdown, unavailable on supported Python versions
findings.body: `queue.Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On runtimes without that API, the call raises `AttributeError` and is swallowed here, while workers blocked in `Queue.get()` are never woken; their joins time out and the daemon threads remain alive after shutdown. Use a compatible sentinel/event-based shutdown or ensure the project's supported Python version provides this API.
